task_instance: Act as the Swedish YouTube & Podcast Mentor for the request 'I moved to Stockholm last month, I know some Swedish, help me get better.' (the skill's own worked mini-example): narrow the vague self-label to an approximate CEFR level, build a listening-first A2 learning path across listening/speaking/writing/reading, and give 3-6 concrete recommendations each with a real, verified clickable link and an explanation of how it helps.
evidence: Produced the full mentor deliverable in mentor_session.md: CEFR-narrowing questions, an A2 listening-first learning path table (listening/speaking/writing/reading with next milestones), and 4 concrete recommendations (Radio Sweden pa latt svenska, Latt Svenska med Oskar, Klartext, Peter SFI) each with a markdown link, level tag, and an explanation of how it serves the target skill, plus a closing micro-win, matching SKILL.md steps 1-12 and the worked mini-example. Verified every link was real (not invented, per the skill's explicit anti-pattern) via WebSearch before including it: 'Radio Sweden pa latt svenska' resolved to https://www.sverigesradio.se/radio-sweden-pa-latt-svenska (corroborated by Sveriges Radio's own site plus Apple Podcasts/Listen Notes/Podnews listings); 'Klartext' resolved to https://www.sverigesradio.se/klartext (corroborated similarly); 'Latt Svenska med Oskar' resolved to https://www.youtube.com/@LattSvenskaMedOskar (matches the channel's own handle in YouTube search results and its Patreon posts); 'Peter SFI' resolved to https://www.youtube.com/@petersfi6089 (matches a news article on the channel's 100k-subscriber milestone). A direct WebFetch of www.sverigesradio.se to double-check page content was blocked by the sandbox's network egress proxy (EGRESS_BLOCKED), but this was a redundant verification step, not a blocker to the deliverable, since WebSearch already corroborated each URL from multiple independent sources. Files produced: mentor_session.md (the full mentor response + verification notes) and result.json, both in the work directory.
